tagline.en: No money. No knowledge. One grandmother with very thick glasses.

persona.en: A tenant-farming family in Mallepalli, a cotton village in Telangana. Nobody in the house has a bank account, and the kirana shop's khata is always open.

role.en: Your grandmother. Thick glasses, tied with black thread. Calls you kanna.
Your little sister. Wants to be a nurse. Copies everything you do.
Your best friend. Funny, generous, always in a hurry.
A smooth talker from town. His sunglasses get bigger every visit.
An agent who sells whatever pays the best commission. Arrives at lunchtime.
Your father, Yadagiri. Farms two rented acres. Scared of paperwork.
Your mother, Saroja. Field worker, savings-group member, mental-maths champion.
Runs the kirana shop. Her khata notebook remembers everything.
The village moneylender. Polite, patient, very expensive.
Your school teacher. Turns every problem into a sum.
The Bank Mitra and savings-group leader. Her bank office is also a tailoring shop.
The family buffalo. Survives everything. Judges everyone.

text.en: Mallepalli. One kirana shop, one bus a day, and one big tank that floods or dries up.
Your family rents two acres. {cast:father} grows cotton. {cast:mother} works in other people's fields.
Nobody in your house has ever been inside a bank. The kirana [[khata]] is always open.
Everyone says the family lost Thatha's land the year the rains failed. Ammamma never says anything at all.
You are 11. You have ₹50, a little sister called {cast:sibling}, and a best friend called {cast:friend}.
Kanna, money is like water. Plan where it goes, or it goes wherever it likes.
I know this story well. I was there for all of it. Let's begin.
Shares his father's OTP for free game gems. Loses ₹2,500 in a minute.
Buys a phone on EMI. Pays ₹9,588 for a ₹7,500 phone.
Downloads a betting app. Wins ₹300, then loses ₹6,000 chasing it.
Drops out and follows Lucky Prakash to the city for quick cash.
Borrows from three loan apps to repay one. Recovery agents call his mother.
His bank account is frozen as a money mule. He calls 1930 and tells the truth.
Delivery rider. Saves ₹1,000 a month in an RD. Laughs again.
Opens a mobile repair stall with a Mudra loan. His dream is six years late, but real.
